data.title: Snack Safari: Adding and Subtracting to 5
data.subject: Math
data.overview: Turn snack time or toy time into an interactive math safari! Learners explore early addition and subtraction within 5 by moving tangible objects across plates, discovering how groups change when we combine or take away.
learningObjectives: Model addition equations up to 5 by joining two groups of objects.
Demonstrate subtraction within 5 by physically taking objects away from a whole group.
Explain how adding makes a group larger and subtracting makes a group smaller.

materials.item: Paper plate or sheet of plain paper

substitutes: piece of yarn to divide plate

steps.title: Create the Safari Zones
steps.instruction: Use a crayon to draw a line straight down the middle of your paper plate to divide it into two sides: Safari Grassland and Safari Jungle.
steps.tip: If using a placemat, you can place a piece of yarn or string right down the middle instead of drawing. Checkpoint: Check that you clearly see two distinct sides.

steps.title: Count Your Safari Herd
steps.instruction: Count out exactly 5 counters and place them beside your plate. Touch each counter as you count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

checkpoint.question: Do you have exactly 5 counters in your herd?

steps.tip: Line the counters in a straight row so it is easy to touch-count each one without double-counting.

steps.title: Explore Grouping (Part-Part-Whole)
steps.instruction: Place 2 counters on the Safari Grassland side and 3 counters on the Safari Jungle side. Push both groups together into the center to see how many you have in total.

checkpoint.question: How many total counters do you have when 2 join with 3?

steps.scienceNote: Addition means joining two or more groups together to make a larger total group.

steps.title: Discover a New Number Pair
steps.instruction: Separate the counters again, but this time put 4 counters on one side and 1 counter on the other side. Slide them together again and count the total.
steps.tip: Help your child notice that 5 can be made from different pairs (2 and 3, or 4 and 1).

steps.title: Act Out Subtraction (Taking Away)
steps.instruction: Start with all 5 counters together on your plate. Your stuffed animal is hungry or wants to drive away! Move 2 counters off the plate and drop them into your small cup.

checkpoint.question: How many counters are still remaining on the plate?

steps.scienceNote: Subtraction means removing items from a group, which leaves us with a smaller amount than when we started.

steps.title: The Disappearing Animal Game
steps.instruction: Have your adult partner cover some of the 5 counters with the cup while your eyes are closed. Open your eyes, count the counters left on the plate, and guess how many are hidden in the cup.

checkpoint.question: Can you explain how you knew how many were hiding under the cup?

steps.tip: Encourage holding up fingers to represent the total 5 to help figure out the missing part.

reflectionPrompts.question: When we pushed counters from both sides of the plate into the center, did our group get bigger or smaller?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Model addition equations up to 5 by joining two groups of objects.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about whether having 2 items and getting 3 more gives you more items than you started with.

reflectionPrompts.question: When the stuffed animal took crackers off the plate, what happened to the number left on the plate?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Demonstrate subtraction within 5 by physically taking objects away from a whole group.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Look at the plate before and after the crackers were put in the cup.

reflectionPrompts.question: Can you think of a time at home when you add things together or take things away?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Explain how adding makes a group larger and subtracting makes a group smaller.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about sharing snacks, cleaning up toys into a toy box, or adding blocks to a tower.

documentationPrompt.instruction: Take a photo of your plate showing your favorite way to make 5 with counters, or draw your plate on paper.
documentationPrompt.suggestedCaption: Today on my Snack Safari, I discovered that [number] plus [number] equals 5!

extensions.title: Five-Frame Detective
extensions.description: Draw a 1x5 grid (a five-frame) on paper. Place counters in the boxes one by one to see visually how many boxes are filled and how many empty boxes are left to reach 5.

extensions.title: Story Problem Creator
extensions.description: Invent your own short math story aloud using toys or snacks (e.g., 'Three cars were parked, and two zoomed in. How many are there now?').

safetyNotes: Adult helper recommended for kindergarten learners.
Small objects such as buttons or small toys can present a choking hazard; ensure young learners do not place non-food counters in their mouths.
If using edible crackers, make sure hands and work surfaces are clean before the activity.

cards.title: Plus Sign
cards.definition: The plus sign means we put things together to make more.
cards.timelineContext: When counting starts, plus brings items together.
cards.originStory: People crossed two lines to show things joining up!
cards.curiosityNote: It looks just like a tiny crossroads or a bandage!
cards.visualPrompt: A bright green friendly plus sign hugging two red apples and two green apples together on a clean white background, vector storybook style.

cards.title: Minus Sign
cards.definition: The minus sign means we take things away.
cards.timelineContext: Next, minus shows when items roll away.
cards.originStory: A little flat line was drawn to show something left!
cards.curiosityNote: It looks like a straight stick taking a nap!
cards.visualPrompt: A friendly bright blue minus sign with cartoon eyes watching one cookie roll away from a plate of five cookies, playful storybook illustration.

cards.title: Equals Sign
cards.definition: The equals sign shows both sides have the exact same amount.

conceptElements.detail: Two lines stacked like matching tracks.
conceptElements.label: Twin Lines

cards.timelineContext: At the end, equals tells the whole story.
cards.originStory: A clever teacher drew two twin lines because nothing is more equal!
cards.curiosityNote: The two bars look like two little train tracks!
cards.visualPrompt: A cheerful bright purple equals sign balancing two yellow stars on the left and two yellow stars on the right, simple kindergarten picture book style.

concepts.name: Plus Sign
concepts.briefDefinition: The plus sign looks like a cross and means adding more.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The bright green cross between the two added numbers

inContext.scenario: You have two toy cars and get one more car.
inContext.whereToFind: The plus sign shows we are putting cars together.

selfCheck.prompt: Which sign looks like a cross and adds more?
selfCheck.hint: Look for the sign shaped like two crossed lines.

concepts.name: Minus Sign
concepts.briefDefinition: The minus sign is one flat line that takes away.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The bright blue flat line between the subtracted numbers

inContext.scenario: You have three sweet cookies and eat one up.
inContext.whereToFind: The minus sign shows we took one cookie away.

selfCheck.prompt: Which sign is one flat line that takes away?
selfCheck.hint: Look for just one straight sleeping line.

concepts.name: Equals Sign
concepts.briefDefinition: The equals sign has two lines and shows the total.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The two amber flat lines right before the answer

inContext.scenario: You count all your blocks to find the total number.
inContext.whereToFind: The equals sign sits right in front of the answer.

selfCheck.prompt: Which sign has two flat lines stacked together?
selfCheck.hint: Look for two matching flat lines on top of each other.
